title: Characterisation of human penile tissue properties using experimental testing combined with multi-target inverse finite element modelling
parameter_location: Table 1, printed page 233; equations 1–3, printed page 229; Table 3, printed page 234

cohort.preparation: fresh-frozen, stored at -20 C; defrosted and tested in PBS at 37 +/- 2 C

estimate_kind: published multi-target inverse finite-element fitted point estimates

corpus_cavernosum.evidence: whole-organ inverse fit assessed against individual radial compression; no glans assignment

corpus_spongiosum.evidence: effective whole CS including urethra plate-compression fit; no independent uniaxial layer data

fascia.evidence: whole-organ inverse fit with assumed neo-Hookean law; no individual fascia experimental data

tunica_albuginea.evidence: single circumferential fiber family approximation; user must supply a reference-space fiber direction

limitations: Small elderly ex vivo cohort; no generic adult or subject-specific calibration claim.
No fitted glans, skin, tendon, ligament or arbitrary organ coefficients.
Fascia had no independent specimen data; CS fit includes the urethra.
Compressibility was not independently measured in confined compression.
TA single circumferential family is a paper assumption, not a measured full collagen architecture.
No viscoelasticity, damage, active tone, perfusion or poroelastic pressure fit.

The paper prints D2=0 although its general equation contains 1/D2. This implementation interprets zero as an omitted higher-order volumetric term; native Abaqus runtime parity has not been established.
Point estimates have no reported joint covariance; fit residuals are not parameter confidence intervals.
